# Introduction

Differential abundance (DA) identifies *where* in state-space the mutant mouse cells are enriched or depleted relative to wildtype. However, it does not explain *what* is driving the cells into these cell states. This notebook bridges the two views by finding genes and gene-sets whose activity is associated with the abundance shift. To this end, I used two approaches:

-   Rank co-enriched and co-depleted genes by regressing per-neighbourhood average gene expression on the neighbourhood log fold-change.

-   Identify shift-associated by running GSEA on the ranked genes identifies pathways whose activity is associated with the pattern of DA.

# Helper functions

```{r helpers}
nhood_sizes <- function(milo) colSums(nhoods(milo))

lfc_precision_weights <- function(da.res, milo,
                                  use = c("size", "fdr", "both")) {
  use  <- match.arg(use)
  sz   <- nhood_sizes(milo)[da.res$Nhood]
  w_size <- sz / stats::median(sz)
  if (use == "size") return(w_size)
  w_fdr <- pmin(-log10(pmax(da.res$SpatialFDR, 1e-12)), 8)
  w_fdr <- w_fdr / stats::median(w_fdr[is.finite(w_fdr)])
  if (use == "fdr") return(w_fdr)
  sqrt(w_size * w_fdr)
}

build_substrate <- function(milo, da.res,
                            assay      = "logcounts",
                            subset.row = NULL,
                            weight_by  = c("both", "size", "fdr")) {
  weight_by <- match.arg(weight_by)
  milo <- calcNhoodExpression(milo, assay = assay, subset.row = subset.row)
  X    <- as.matrix(nhoodExpression(milo))          # genes × nhoods
  X    <- X[, da.res$Nhood, drop = FALSE]           # align to da.res row order
  colnames(X) <- da.res$Nhood #?
  y    <- da.res$logFC
  w    <- lfc_precision_weights(da.res, milo, use = weight_by)
  keep <- matrixStats::rowVars(X) > 0               # drop all-zero genes
  list(milo = milo, X = X[keep, , drop = FALSE], y = y, w = w,
       genes = rownames(X)[keep], da.res = da.res)
}

pergene_lfc_regression <- function(sub) {
  design <- stats::model.matrix(~ sub$y)
  colnames(design) <- c("(Intercept)", "LFC")
  fit <- limma::lmFit(sub$X, design, weights = sub$w)
  fit <- limma::eBayes(fit, trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)
  tt  <- limma::topTable(fit, coef = "LFC", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
  data.frame(
    gene  = rownames(tt),
    slope = tt$logFC,     # slope of nhood expression on nhood logFC
    t     = tt$t,
    P     = tt$P.Value,
    FDR   = tt$adj.P.Val,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

build_detection_substrate <- function(milo, da.res, subset.row = NULL) {
  # binary detection matrix without coercion headaches: keep nonzeros, set to 1
  Dbin <- Matrix::drop0(SingleCellExperiment::counts(milo))
  Dbin@x <- rep(1, length(Dbin@x))                 # genes x cells, 1 = detected
  if (!is.null(subset.row)) Dbin <- Dbin[intersect(subset.row, rownames(Dbin)), , drop = FALSE]
  nh   <- nhoods(milo)                             # cells x nhoods (binary)
  k    <- as.matrix(Dbin %*% nh)                   # genes x nhoods: cells expressing
  storage.mode(k) <- "double"
  nvec <- as.numeric(Matrix::colSums(nh))          # cells per nhood
 
  # depth covariate: per-nhood mean log library size. Detection is monotone in
  # library size, so a depth gradient aligned with LFC would fake a positive
  # slope on every gene -> regress it out.
  libsize  <- Matrix::colSums(SingleCellExperiment::counts(milo))
  nh_depth <- as.vector(Matrix::crossprod(nh, log1p(libsize)) / nvec)
 
  ord <- da.res$Nhood
  structure(
    list(k     = k[, ord, drop = FALSE],
         n     = nvec[ord],
         depth = as.numeric(scale(nh_depth[ord])), # centred+scaled for conditioning
         lfc   = da.res$logFC,
         genes = rownames(k)),
    nhood_order = ord)                             # for permutation-null alignment
}

.fit_detection_glm <- function(kg, n, covdf) {
  Y <- cbind(kg, n - kg)                           # two-column binomial response
  fit <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(stats::glm(Y ~ ., data = covdf, family = stats::quasibinomial())),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  na <- c(log_or = NA, odds_ratio = NA, se = NA, t = NA, P = NA,
          dispersion = NA, converged = 0, separation = NA)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(na)
  sm <- summary(fit)                               # <- SE, t, p, dispersion all from base R
  co <- sm$coefficients
  if (!"LFC" %in% rownames(co)) return(na)
  sep <- any(fit$fitted.values < 1e-8 | fit$fitted.values > 1 - 1e-8)  # perfect separation
  c(log_or     = unname(co["LFC", "Estimate"]),
    odds_ratio = unname(exp(co["LFC", "Estimate"])),
    se         = unname(co["LFC", "Std. Error"]),
    t          = unname(co["LFC", "t value"]),
    P          = unname(co["LFC", "Pr(>|t|)"]),
    dispersion = unname(sm$dispersion),
    converged  = as.numeric(isTRUE(fit$converged)),
    separation = as.numeric(sep))
}

detection_lfc_model <- function(sub,
                                adjust_depth      = TRUE,
                                min_detect_nhoods = 5L,
                                max_mean_frac     = 0.95,
                                min_mean_frac     = 0.005,
                                genes             = NULL,
                                BPPARAM           = NULL,
                                batch_size        = 500L) {
  k <- sub$k; n <- sub$n
  if (!is.null(genes)) k <- k[intersect(genes, rownames(k)), , drop = FALSE]

  tot_n     <- sum(n)
  mean_frac <- Matrix::rowSums(k) / tot_n
  n_detect  <- Matrix::rowSums(k > 0)

  ceiling_g <- rownames(k)[mean_frac > max_mean_frac]
  eligible  <- rownames(k)[n_detect >= min_detect_nhoods &
                           mean_frac <= max_mean_frac &
                           mean_frac >= min_mean_frac]

  covdf   <- if (adjust_depth) data.frame(LFC = sub$lfc, depth = sub$depth)
             else              data.frame(LFC = sub$lfc)
  n_cores <- if (!is.null(BPPARAM)) BPPARAM else 1L

  # Batch genes so each mclapply fork only inherits a small k slice.
  # batch_size = Inf disables batching (one mclapply over all genes) — safe on high-RAM machines.
  # batch_size = 500 reduces per-fork memory at the cost of serial overhead between batches.
  bs <- if (is.infinite(batch_size)) length(eligible) else as.integer(batch_size)
  batches <- split(eligible, ceiling(seq_along(eligible) / bs))
  rows <- unlist(lapply(batches, function(batch) {
    k_b <- k[batch, , drop = FALSE]
    fit_b <- function(g) .fit_detection_glm(k_b[g, ], n, covdf)
    if (n_cores > 1L)
      parallel::mclapply(batch, fit_b, mc.cores = n_cores)
    else
      lapply(batch, fit_b)
  }), recursive = FALSE)

  M <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  res <- data.frame(gene = eligible, M,
                    mean_frac   = mean_frac[eligible],
                    n_detect_nh = n_detect[eligible],
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  res <- res[stats::complete.cases(res[, c("t", "P")]), ]
  res$FDR <- stats::p.adjust(res$P, "BH")
  res <- res[order(-res$t), ]
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  list(result  = res,
       ceiling = data.frame(gene = ceiling_g,
                            mean_frac = mean_frac[ceiling_g],
                            stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}

make_detection_stat_fun <- function(sub, candidate_genes, adjust_depth = TRUE) {
  k     <- sub$k[candidate_genes, , drop = FALSE]   # cols follow nhood_order
  n     <- sub$n
  depth <- sub$depth
  ord   <- attr(sub, "nhood_order")
  function(da_perm) {
    lfc   <- da_perm$logFC[match(ord, da_perm$Nhood)]   # align permuted LFC to substrate
    covdf <- if (adjust_depth) data.frame(LFC = lfc, depth = depth)
             else              data.frame(LFC = lfc)
    vapply(rownames(k),
           function(g) .fit_detection_glm(k[g, ], n, covdf)[["t"]],
           numeric(1))
  }
}
enrichment_fgsea <- function(gene_stat_df, gene_sets, stat = "t",
                             minSize = 15, maxSize = 500, eps = 0) {
  ranks <- gene_stat_df[[stat]]
  names(ranks) <- gene_stat_df$gene
  ranks <- sort(ranks[is.finite(ranks)], decreasing = TRUE)
  res   <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(pathways = gene_sets, stats = ranks,
                                  minSize = minSize, maxSize = maxSize, eps = eps)
  res[order(res$padj), ]
}

load_msig_mouse <- function(collection, subcollection = NULL) {
  if (!requireNamespace("msigdbr", quietly = TRUE)) stop("install msigdbr")
  h <- msigdbr::msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus",
                        collection = collection,
                        subcollection = subcollection)
  split(h$gene_symbol, h$gs_name)
}
```

# DA landscape

The output of MiloR DA is visualized below on a neighbourhood graph coloured by DA logFC comparing condition (mCh+ or mCh- ) to WT control (blue = depleted, red = enriched). The neighbourhood is an aggregated view of the cell nearest neighbour graph. The embedding of node is the median UMAP coordinates of the memeber cells. Each node is a neighbourhood; size reflects neighbourhood size.

::: panel-tabset
## Het mCh+ vs WT

```{r da-landscape-pos, fig.height=6, fig.width=10}
  labs(title = milo_hsc_da$mChPos_vs_WT$model_contrast, fill = "log2FC",
```

# Continuous per-gene expression on LFC regression using limma

Regress neighbourhood-averaged expression on neighbourhood LFC using limma (weighted by miloR FDR). Both contrasts share the same neighbourhood expression matrix, computed once.

```{r build-substrate}
milo_hsc_obj <- calcNhoodExpression(milo_hsc_obj, assay = "logcounts", subset.row = gene_subset)
nhexpr       <- as.matrix(nhoodExpression(milo_hsc_obj))   # genes × nhoods

build_sub_expr <- function(nhexpr, da.res, milo, weight_by = "fdr") {
  X    <- nhexpr[, da.res$Nhood, drop = FALSE]
  y    <- da.res$logFC
  w    <- lfc_precision_weights(da.res, milo, use = weight_by)
  keep <- matrixStats::rowVars(X) > 0
  list(X = X[keep, , drop = FALSE], y = y, w = w, genes = rownames(X)[keep])
}

sub_pos <- build_sub_expr(nhexpr, da_res_pos, milo_hsc_obj)
sub_neg <- build_sub_expr(nhexpr, da_res_neg, milo_hsc_obj)
```

```{r pergene-lfc-reg}
gstats_pos <- pergene_lfc_regression(sub_pos)
gstats_neg <- pergene_lfc_regression(sub_neg)
```

```{r limma-rank-helper}
# ── labelling helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
label_limma_rank <- function(gstats, n = 10) {
  gstats %>%
    mutate(sig       = FDR < SIG_FDR,
           direction = case_when(sig & slope > 0 ~ "Co-enriched",
                                 sig & slope < 0 ~ "Co-depleted",
                                 TRUE            ~ "NS")) %>%
    filter(sig) %>% group_by(direction) %>%
    slice_max(abs(t), n = n) %>% ungroup()
}

# ── pure plotting function ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plot_limma_rank <- function(gstats, labels = NULL, title = "") {
  df <- gstats %>%
    mutate(sig       = FDR < SIG_FDR,
           direction = case_when(sig & slope > 0 ~ "Co-enriched",
                                 sig & slope < 0 ~ "Co-depleted",
                                 TRUE            ~ "NS"),
           rank = rank(-t))
  n_genes <- nrow(df)
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = rank, y = t)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = direction), size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = dir_cols, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Gene rank", y = "t-statistic (limma slope ~ nhood logFC)", title = title) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13)
  if (!is.null(labels) && nrow(labels) > 0) {
    label_df <- df %>% filter(gene %in% labels$gene)
    nudge    <- ifelse(label_df$direction == "Co-enriched", n_genes * 0.12, -n_genes * 0.12)
    p <- p + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = label_df, aes(label = gene, colour = direction),
      size = 3.5, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE,
      nudge_x = nudge, segment.size = 0.25, segment.colour = "grey55")
  }
  p
}

scatter_gene <- function(sub, gene, contrast_label) {
  data.frame(t(sub$X), y = sub$y) %>%
    ggplot(aes(!!sym(gene), y)) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = y), shape = 21, size = 2, stroke = 0.3, colour = "black", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", name = "DA log2FC") +
    xlab(paste(gene, "neighbourhood-averaged expression")) +
    ylab(paste("MiloR DA log2FC", contrast_label)) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11)
}
```

### Het mCh+ vs WT {.unnumbered}

The expression of the top ranked -based on the order of the model's t-test statistic- gene tracks the abundance shift quite well.

However, it penalizes interesting candidates like Meis2 (ranked 215), which we observed that its expression pattern is co-enriched in mutant-mouse enriched states. Interestingly, although the expression of Meis2 is clearly co-enriched with mCh+ cells, it displays a switch-like expression pattern instead of a continuous one like Bhlhe40.

Despite the ability to capture genes that track the abundance shift, this result shows the limitation of modeling LogFC by regressing over the continuous neighbourhood expression using limma. Namely, it rewards genes that are expressed in larger number of neighborhoods because they're more likely to continuously track with the differential abundance pattern. Thus, it could bias against genes that are exclusively expressed in the differentially abundant state. This will be addressed using a "detection" model in the next section.

```{r limma-scatter-pos, fig.width=12, fig.height=4}
top_gene_pos <- gstats_pos$gene[which.max(gstats_pos$t)]
scatter_gene(sub_pos, top_gene_pos, "(mCh+)") + scatter_gene(sub_pos, "Meis2", "(mCh+)")
```

### Comparison: mCh+ vs mCh- {.unnumbered}

<details>

<summary>t-statistic scatter & condition-differential rank — mCh+ vs mCh- (click to expand)</summary>

Genes significant in both contrasts at the same direction are **Shared**; opposite directions are **Discordant**; unique to one contrast are labelled by condition.

```{r limma-compare, fig.height=6, fig.width=14}
cmp_lim <- inner_join(
  gstats_pos %>% select(gene, t_pos = t, FDR_pos = FDR),
  gstats_neg %>% select(gene, t_neg = t, FDR_neg = FDR),
  by = "gene"
) %>%
  mutate(
    delta = t_pos - t_neg,          # positive = stronger mCh+ effect, negative = stronger mCh-
    sig   = FDR_pos < SIG_FDR | FDR_neg < SIG_FDR
  )

# Label: top 10 per condition extremes + top 10 shared in each direction
lim_lab <- bind_rows(
  cmp_lim %>% filter(sig) %>% slice_max(delta, n = 10),            # most mCh+ dominant
  cmp_lim %>% filter(sig) %>% slice_min(delta, n = 10),            # most mCh- dominant
  cmp_lim %>% filter(sig, t_pos > 0, t_neg > 0) %>% slice_max(t_pos + t_neg, n = 10),  # shared enriched
  cmp_lim %>% filter(sig, t_pos < 0, t_neg < 0) %>% slice_max(-(t_pos + t_neg), n = 10) # shared depleted
) %>% distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)

p_lim_scatter <- ggplot(cmp_lim, aes(t_pos, t_neg)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = delta), shape = 21, colour = "grey30", size = 1.5, stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lim_lab, aes(label = gene),
                           size = 2.8, colour = "grey20", max.overlaps = Inf,
                           segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey55") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       name = "Δt (mCh+ − mCh-)") +
  labs(x = "t-statistic (mCh+ vs WT)", y = "t-statistic (mCh- vs WT)",
       title = "Limma — mCh+ vs mCh- (scatter)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)

# Rank plot by delta among significant genes
lim_rank <- cmp_lim %>% filter(sig) %>% arrange(desc(delta)) %>% mutate(rank = row_number())
n_sig_lim <- nrow(lim_rank)
lim_rank_lab <- bind_rows(slice_max(lim_rank, delta, n = 15), slice_min(lim_rank, delta, n = 15)) %>%
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)
nudge_lim <- ifelse(lim_rank_lab$delta > 0, n_sig_lim * 0.08, -n_sig_lim * 0.08)

p_lim_rank <- ggplot(lim_rank, aes(rank, delta)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = delta), shape = 21, colour = "grey30", size = 1.5, stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lim_rank_lab, aes(label = gene),
                           size = 2.8, colour = "grey20", max.overlaps = Inf,
                           nudge_x = nudge_lim,
                           segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey55") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       name = "Δt (mCh+ − mCh-)") +
  labs(x = "Gene rank", y = "Δt (mCh+ − mCh-)",
       title = "Limma — condition-differential rank",
       caption = "Ranked by mCh+ − mCh- t-stat; labelled: top 15 at each extreme") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)

p_lim_scatter | p_lim_rank
```


</details>

# Per-gene detection regression

To address the limitation of limma continuous model from the previous section, we use a model that uses the per-neighborhood "detection" of a gene instead of its average expression.

```{r fit-quasibinomial}
sub_det_pos <- build_detection_substrate(milo_hsc_obj, da_res_pos, subset.row = gene_subset)

# Reuse k/n/depth from pos; swap lfc for neg aligned to the same nhood order
ord_pos       <- attr(sub_det_pos, "nhood_order")
sub_det_neg   <- sub_det_pos
sub_det_neg$lfc <- da_res_neg$logFC[match(ord_pos, da_res_neg$Nhood)]

n_cores <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 2L)
det_pos <- detection_lfc_model(sub_det_pos, adjust_depth = TRUE, BPPARAM = n_cores)
det_neg <- detection_lfc_model(sub_det_neg, adjust_depth = TRUE, BPPARAM = n_cores)
```

```{r det-rank-helper}
# ── labelling helpers — called explicitly in each chunk ──────────────────────

label_det_rank <- function(det_res, n = 10) {
  det_res %>%
    mutate(sig       = FDR < SIG_FDR,
           direction = case_when(sig & log_or > 0 ~ "Co-enriched",
                                 sig & log_or < 0 ~ "Co-depleted",
                                 TRUE             ~ "NS")) %>%
    filter(sig) %>% group_by(direction) %>%
    slice_max(abs(log_or), n = n) %>% ungroup()
}

label_det_volcano <- function(det_res, n = 20) {
  det_res %>%
    filter(FDR < SIG_FDR) %>%
    mutate(direction = if_else(log_or > 0, "Co-enriched", "Co-depleted")) %>%
    group_by(direction) %>%
    slice_max(abs(log_or), n = n) %>%
    ungroup()
}

label_det_frac_lor <- function(det_res, n_bins = 20, n_per_bin = 2) {
  # Bin mean_frac; within each bin × direction take top n_per_bin by abs(log_or)
  det_res %>%
    filter(FDR < SIG_FDR) %>%
    mutate(
      direction = if_else(log_or > 0, "Co-enriched", "Co-depleted"),
      frac_bin  = cut(mean_frac, breaks = n_bins, labels = FALSE)
    ) %>%
    group_by(direction, frac_bin) %>%
    slice_max(abs(log_or), n = n_per_bin) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# ── pure plotting functions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

plot_det_rank <- function(det_res, labels = NULL, title = "") {
  df <- det_res %>%
    mutate(rank      = rank(-log_or),
           sig       = FDR < SIG_FDR,
           direction = case_when(sig & log_or > 0 ~ "Co-enriched",
                                 sig & log_or < 0 ~ "Co-depleted",
                                 TRUE             ~ "NS"))
  n_genes <- nrow(df)
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = rank, y = log_or)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = mean_frac), size = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "turbo", direction = -1,
                           name = "mean frac\n(↓ = localized)") +
    labs(x = "Gene rank", y = "log Odds Ratio", title = title) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13)
  if (!is.null(labels) && nrow(labels) > 0) {
    label_df <- df %>% filter(gene %in% labels$gene)
    nudge    <- ifelse(label_df$direction == "Co-enriched", n_genes * 0.12, -n_genes * 0.12)
    p <- p + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = label_df, aes(label = gene), colour = "grey20",
      size = 3.5, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE,
      nudge_x = nudge, segment.size = 0.25, segment.colour = "grey55")
  }
  p
}

plot_det_volcano <- function(det_res, labels = NULL, title = "") {
  # FDR=0 genes: place at -log10(double.xmin) ~308 so they sit at the natural top
  df <- det_res %>%
    mutate(sig = FDR < SIG_FDR,
           nlp = -log10(pmax(FDR, .Machine$double.xmin)))
  n_fdr0 <- sum(det_res$FDR == 0)
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(log_or, nlp)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = mean_frac), size = 0.9, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(SIG_FDR), colour = "grey50",
               linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "turbo", direction = -1,
                           name = "mean frac\n(↓ = localized)") +
    labs(x = "log Odds Ratio", y = expression(-log[10](FDR)), title = title,
         caption = paste0(n_fdr0, " FDR = 0 genes at top — also shown in lollipop below")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  if (!is.null(labels) && nrow(labels) > 0) {
    label_df <- df %>% filter(gene %in% labels$gene)
    p <- p + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = label_df, aes(label = gene),
      colour = "grey20", size = 2.8, max.overlaps = Inf,
      segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey55")
  }
  p
}

plot_det_zero_fdr <- function(df, title = "") {
  # df: pre-filtered data frame (caller applies FDR == 0 and any |log_or| threshold)
  df <- df %>% arrange(log_or) %>% mutate(gene = factor(gene, levels = gene))
  ggplot(df, aes(log_or, gene)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = log_or, y = gene, yend = gene),
                 colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = mean_frac), size = 1.5) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "turbo", direction = -1,
                           name = "mean frac\n(↓ = localized)") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(x = "log Odds Ratio", y = NULL, title = title,
         subtitle = paste0(nrow(df), " genes with FDR = 0 & |log OR| ≥ 0.15  —  ordered by log OR")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 5),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor   = element_blank())
}

plot_det_frac_lor <- function(det_res, labels = NULL, title = "") {
  df <- det_res %>%
    mutate(sig = FDR < SIG_FDR,
           nlp = pmin(-log10(FDR + .Machine$double.eps), 10))
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(mean_frac, log_or)) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = nlp), shape = 21, colour = "grey60", size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = 1,
                         name = expression(-log[10](FDR)),
                         limits = c(0, 10), oob = scales::squish) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
    labs(x = "Mean detection fraction", y = "log Odds Ratio", title = title,
         caption = "Labelled: low frac + high |OR| — localized, co-varying genes") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13)
  if (!is.null(labels) && nrow(labels) > 0) {
    label_df <- df %>% filter(gene %in% labels$gene)
    p <- p + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = label_df, aes(label = gene), colour = "grey20",
      size = 2.8, max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = 0,
      segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey55")
  }
  p
}

plot_det_frac_lor_zoomed <- function(df, title = "") {
  # Scatter limited to lollipop genes: label all with direct geom_text (no repel)
  df <- df %>% mutate(nlp = pmin(-log10(FDR + .Machine$double.eps), 10))
  ggplot(df, aes(mean_frac, log_or)) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = nlp), shape = 21, colour = "grey60", size = 3) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = gene), size = 2.0, colour = "grey20",
                             max.overlaps = Inf, force = 0.2, force_pull = 0.9,
                             box.padding = 0.12, segment.size = 0.15, segment.colour = "grey55",
                             min.segment.length = 0) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = 1,
                         name = expression(-log[10](FDR)),
                         limits = c(0, 10), oob = scales::squish) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
    labs(x = "Mean detection fraction", y = "log Odds Ratio", title = title,
         subtitle = paste0(nrow(df), " genes — FDR = 0 & |log OR| ≥ 0.15 — zoom to inspect")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13)
}
```

<summary>FDR = 0 genes — lollipop (click to expand)</summary>

Genes reaching FDR = 0 (numerical machine precision — strongest possible signal) ranked by their log Odds Ratio. Positive OR indicates co-enrichment with DA-enriched neighbourhoods; negative OR indicates co-depletion. Point colour shows mean detection fraction across all neighbourhoods — lower values (dark) mark genes detected only in a small proportion of cells, highlighting localized, state-specific candidates.

The same FDR = 0 genes plotted as mean detection fraction (x) versus log Odds Ratio (y). Restricting to these extreme-significance genes reduces overplotting enough to label all points. ### Comparison: mCh+ vs mCh- {.unnumbered}

```{r det-compare, fig.height=6, fig.width=14}
cmp_det <- inner_join(
  det_pos$result %>% select(gene, lor_pos = log_or, FDR_pos = FDR),
  det_neg$result %>% select(gene, lor_neg = log_or, FDR_neg = FDR),
  by = "gene"
) %>%
  mutate(
    delta = lor_pos - lor_neg,
    sig   = FDR_pos < SIG_FDR | FDR_neg < SIG_FDR
  )

det_lab <- bind_rows(
  cmp_det %>% filter(sig) %>% slice_max(delta, n = 10),
  cmp_det %>% filter(sig) %>% slice_min(delta, n = 10),
  cmp_det %>% filter(sig, lor_pos > 0, lor_neg > 0) %>% slice_max(lor_pos + lor_neg, n = 10),
  cmp_det %>% filter(sig, lor_pos < 0, lor_neg < 0) %>% slice_max(-(lor_pos + lor_neg), n = 10)
) %>% distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)

p_det_scatter <- ggplot(cmp_det, aes(lor_pos, lor_neg)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = delta), shape = 21, colour = "grey30", size = 1.5, stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = det_lab, aes(label = gene),
                           size = 2.8, colour = "grey20", max.overlaps = Inf,
                           segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey55") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       name = "Δ log OR\n(mCh+ − mCh-)") +
  labs(x = "log OR (mCh+ vs WT)", y = "log OR (mCh- vs WT)",
       title = "Detection model — mCh+ vs mCh- (scatter)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)

det_rank <- cmp_det %>% filter(sig) %>% arrange(desc(delta)) %>% mutate(rank = row_number())
n_sig_det <- nrow(det_rank)
det_rank_lab <- bind_rows(slice_max(det_rank, delta, n = 15), slice_min(det_rank, delta, n = 15)) %>%
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)
nudge_det <- ifelse(det_rank_lab$delta > 0, n_sig_det * 0.08, -n_sig_det * 0.08)

p_det_rank <- ggplot(det_rank, aes(rank, delta)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = delta), shape = 21, colour = "grey30", size = 1.5, stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = det_rank_lab, aes(label = gene),
                           size = 2.8, colour = "grey20", max.overlaps = Inf,
                           nudge_x = nudge_det,
                           segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey55") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       name = "Δ log OR\n(mCh+ − mCh-)") +
  labs(x = "Gene rank", y = "Δ log OR (mCh+ − mCh-)",
       title = "Detection model — condition-differential rank",
       caption = "Ranked by mCh+ − mCh- log OR; labelled: top 15 at each extreme") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)

p_det_scatter | p_det_rank
```

```{r det-compare-dl, echo=FALSE}
dl_btn(cmp_det, "det_mchpos_vs_mchneg_comparison.csv",
       "⬇ Download detection model comparison (mCh+ vs mCh-)")
```

# Limma vs detection — method concordance (mCh+)

Both models rank genes by their association with DA, but via slightly different approaches: limma uses continuous neighbourhood-averaged expression; the detection model uses binary detection rates. Genes with switch-like expression pattern score poorly in limma (slope diluted by zero-expression nhoods) but rank highly in the detection model.

```{r limma-vs-det, fig.height=6, fig.width=14}
cmp_methods <- inner_join(
  gstats_pos %>% select(gene, limma_t = t, limma_FDR = FDR),
  det_pos$result %>% select(gene, det_lor = log_or, det_FDR = FDR),
  by = "gene"
) %>%
  mutate(
    sig      = limma_FDR < SIG_FDR | det_FDR < SIG_FDR,
    rank_lim = rank(-limma_t),
    rank_det = rank(-det_lor),
    delta    = rank_det - rank_lim  # positive = detection ranks this gene higher than limma
  )

n_genes <- nrow(cmp_methods)

meth_lab <- bind_rows(
  cmp_methods %>% filter(sig) %>% slice_max(delta,  n = 10),               # detection-biased
  cmp_methods %>% filter(sig) %>% slice_min(delta,  n = 10),               # limma-biased
  cmp_methods %>% filter(sig) %>% slice_min(rank_lim + rank_det, n = 10)   # top concordant
) %>% distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)

p_meth_scatter <- ggplot(cmp_methods, aes(rank_lim, rank_det)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = delta), shape = 21, colour = "grey30", size = 1.5, stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = meth_lab, aes(label = gene), size = 2.5, colour = "grey20",
                           max.overlaps = Inf, segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey55") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       name = "Δrank\n(det − lim)") +
  labs(x = "Limma rank  (1 = highest t)", y = "Detection rank  (1 = highest log OR)",
       title = "Limma vs detection — rank concordance (mCh+ vs WT)",
       caption = "Labelled: top 10 detection-biased, top 10 limma-biased, top 10 concordant  |  dashed = perfect concordance") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)

meth_rank <- cmp_methods %>% filter(sig) %>%
  arrange(desc(delta)) %>% mutate(rank_d = row_number())
n_sig_meth   <- nrow(meth_rank)
meth_rank_lab <- bind_rows(
  slice_max(meth_rank, delta, n = 15),
  slice_min(meth_rank, delta, n = 15)
) %>% distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)
nudge_meth <- ifelse(meth_rank_lab$delta > 0, n_sig_meth * 0.08, -n_sig_meth * 0.08)

p_meth_rank <- ggplot(meth_rank, aes(rank_d, delta)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = delta), shape = 21, colour = "grey30", size = 1.5, stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = meth_rank_lab, aes(label = gene), size = 2.8, colour = "grey20",
                           max.overlaps = Inf, nudge_x = nudge_meth,
                           segment.size = 0.25, segment.colour = "grey55") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       name = "Δrank\n(det − lim)") +
  labs(x = "Gene rank", y = "Δrank  (det − lim)",
       title = "Method-differential rank (mCh+ vs WT)",
       caption = "Significant genes ranked by Δrank; labelled: top 15 at each extreme") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)

p_meth_scatter | p_meth_rank
```

```{r limma-vs-det-stats}
cor_sp <- cor(cmp_methods$rank_lim, cmp_methods$rank_det,
              method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
cat(sprintf("Spearman ρ (limma rank vs detection rank, mCh+): %.3f\n\n", cor_sp))
```

This comparisons highlights some genes that have a much higher rank (i.e. less associated with differential abundance) in limma model compared to the detection model because they either have localized expression in a small part of the cell embedding (e.g  *Fcnb*, and *Clec4a2*) or have as switch-like expression pattern (e.g *Prom1*).

```{r gsea-helpers}
N_TOP_GSEA <- 15
N_TOP_HITS <- 5

render_gsea_tables <- function(gse_results, contrast_tag = "") {
  for (coll_name in names(gse_results)) {
    cat("##", coll_name, "\n\n")
    all_sig <- gse_results[[coll_name]] %>% filter(padj < PADJ_GSEA) %>% arrange(desc(NES))
    if (nrow(all_sig) == 0) { cat("No significant pathways.\n\n"); next }
    # download button for this collection
    fn <- paste0("gsea_", tolower(gsub("[^a-z0-9]", "_", coll_name)), contrast_tag, ".csv")
    print(htmltools::tagList(dl_btn(all_sig, fn,
          paste0("⬇ ", coll_name, " GSEA results (", nrow(all_sig), " sig. pathways)"))))
    cat("\n\n")
    sig <- all_sig %>%
      mutate(pathway     = stringr::str_trunc(abbreviate_pathway(pathway), 60),
             NES         = round(NES, 3),
             padj        = signif(padj, 3),
             leadingEdge = sapply(leadingEdge, \(x) paste(head(x, 8), collapse = ", "))) %>%
      select(pathway, NES, padj, size, leadingEdge)
    print(htmltools::tagList(DT::datatable(sig, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                                          options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))))
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}

render_gsea_bars <- function(gse_results) {
  for (coll_name in names(gse_results)) {
    cat("##", coll_name, "\n\n")
    res <- gse_results[[coll_name]] %>%
      filter(padj < PADJ_GSEA) %>%
      mutate(direction     = if_else(NES > 0, "Co-enriched", "Co-depleted"),
             pathway_short = stringr::str_trunc(abbreviate_pathway(pathway), 55))
    if (nrow(res) == 0) { cat("No significant pathways.\n\n"); next }
    df_dep <- res %>% filter(direction == "Co-depleted") %>%
      slice_max(abs(NES), n = N_TOP_GSEA, with_ties = FALSE) %>% arrange(abs(NES))
    df_enr <- res %>% filter(direction == "Co-enriched") %>%
      slice_max(abs(NES), n = N_TOP_GSEA, with_ties = FALSE) %>% arrange(abs(NES))
    df <- bind_rows(df_dep, df_enr) %>%
      mutate(pathway_short = factor(pathway_short, levels = unique(pathway_short)),
             direction     = factor(direction, levels = c("Co-enriched", "Co-depleted")),
             label_x       = if_else(NES > 0, 0.05, -0.05),
             label_hjust   = if_else(NES > 0, 0, 1))
    p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = NES, y = pathway_short)) +
      geom_col(aes(fill = direction), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_text(aes(label = paste0("p=", signif(padj, 2)), x = label_x, hjust = label_hjust),
                size = 2.5, colour = "grey20") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("Co-enriched" = "#B2182B", "Co-depleted" = "#2166AC"),
                        name = NULL) +
      facet_grid(direction ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
      labs(x = "NES", y = NULL, title = coll_name,
           caption = paste0("Top ", N_TOP_GSEA, " per direction — padj < ", PADJ_GSEA)) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
      theme(legend.position = "none", strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),
            strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
            axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
    print(p)
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}

make_enrich_plots <- function(paths_df, gs_list, ranks_stat) {
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(paths_df)), function(i) {
    pw <- paths_df$pathway[i]
    fgsea::plotEnrichment(gs_list[[pw]], stats = ranks_stat) +
      labs(title    = stringr::str_trunc(abbreviate_pathway(pw), 50),
           subtitle = paste0("NES=", round(paths_df$NES[i], 2),
                             "  padj=", signif(paths_df$padj[i], 2))) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7))
  })
}

render_gsea_curves <- function(gse_results, gs_list, ranks_stat) {
  for (coll_name in names(gse_results)) {
    cat("##", coll_name, "\n\n")
    enr <- gse_results[[coll_name]] %>% filter(padj < PADJ_GSEA, NES > 0) %>%
      arrange(padj) %>% head(N_TOP_HITS)
    dep <- gse_results[[coll_name]] %>% filter(padj < PADJ_GSEA, NES < 0) %>%
      arrange(padj) %>% head(N_TOP_HITS)
    if (nrow(enr) == 0 && nrow(dep) == 0) { cat("No significant pathways.\n\n"); next }
    if (nrow(enr) > 0) {
      cat("**Co-enriched — top", nrow(enr), "pathways**\n\n")
      print(patchwork::wrap_plots(make_enrich_plots(enr, gs_list[[coll_name]], ranks_stat),
                                  ncol = min(nrow(enr), 3)))
      cat("\n\n")
    }
    if (nrow(dep) > 0) {
      cat("**Co-depleted — top", nrow(dep), "pathways**\n\n")
      print(patchwork::wrap_plots(make_enrich_plots(dep, gs_list[[coll_name]], ranks_stat),
                                  ncol = min(nrow(dep), 3)))
      cat("\n\n")
    }
  }
}

ranks_pos <- { r <- det_pos$result$log_or; names(r) <- det_pos$result$gene

               sort(r[is.finite(r)], decreasing = TRUE) }
ranks_cmp <- { r <- cmp_det$delta; names(r) <- cmp_det$gene
               sort(r[is.finite(r)], decreasing = TRUE) }
```

## mCh+ vs mCh- (condition-differential rank) {.unnumbered}

GSEA ranked by the detection-model delta (log OR mCh+ minus log OR mCh-). Positive NES = pathways more strongly co-enriched with mCh+ neighbourhoods than mCh-; negative NES = more strongly co-enriched with mCh- neighbourhoods. The ranking statistic is the same `delta` column from the comparison scatter in the Per-gene detection section above.

# Limitations

-   Very small, disconnected clusters were excluded from the analysis.

-   I modeled the differential abundance pattern globally.

-   I used the logFC from all neighborhoods of the included clusters, regardless of the their p-adj value. Nevertheless, the model uses the corresponding p-adj values as weight.

-   I tested all genes for co-enrichment or co-depletion to avoid neglecting interesting genes that are expressed at low level. However, this means that genes that are not variable enough in the first place are included in the modeling. Nevertheless, these gene are not expected to come up as top hits anyway.

-   The expression values that were used are neighborhood averages, not single-cells.

# Conclusion

We used differential abundance to define enriched and depleted cell states in the mutant mouse with respect to the wild-type control. To identify candidate genes involved in the enrichment or depletion of specific cell states, we modeled the differential abundance score as a function of gene expression using linear models. This allowed us to rank genes based on their positive or negative association with the cell states of interest from the mutant mouse, and highlight the set of active biological processes in them. Importantly, it allowed us to have a deeper look on what sets mCh+ and mCh- apart at the earliest stage. While both share expression of stemness markers like *Mmrn1* (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41568470/), each displays a specific set of gene expression pattern. *Meis2*, *Csf3*, and *Nkx2-3* are more enriched in the mCh+ cells, while mCh- uniquely turns on matricellular-associated genes like *Ccn1* and *Matn4*. These are genes are non-structural component of the ECM that mediates signals between the cell and its environment, and fibroblast regulators. Interestingly, *Ccn1* was shown to promote cell survival in AML by indirectly activating Bcl-xL (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4153307/), which is also up-regulated in the mutant mouse clusters (6 and 8), especially in the mCh- cells.*Matn4* is an ECM component whose expression is specific to LT-HSC and anticorrelates with proliferation towards progenitors (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5030798/).

Top co-enriched genesets per contrast and per MSigDB collection (up to 10 per collection, ranked by padj) scored per cell with UCell and overlaid on the combined HSC UMAP.

```{r gsea-ucell-helpers}
plot_ucell_umap <- function(ucell_df, score_col) {
  df  <- ucell_df[order(ucell_df[[score_col]]), ]
  q99 <- quantile(df[[score_col]], 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)
  ggplot(df, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = .data[[score_col]])) +
    geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "turbo", name = "UCell",
                           limits = c(0, q99), oob = scales::squish) +
    facet_wrap(~ sample.name, nrow = 1) +
    labs(title = score_col) +
    theme_void(base_size = 9) +
    theme(plot.title        = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
          legend.key.height = unit(0.4, "cm"),
          strip.text        = element_text(size = 9))
}

render_ucell_maps <- function(gse_lst, n = 10) {
  for (coll_name in names(gse_lst)) {
    cat("##", coll_name, "\n\n")
    top_df <- gse_lst[[coll_name]] %>%
      filter(padj < PADJ_GSEA, NES > 0) %>%
      arrange(padj) %>%
      slice_head(n = n)
    if (nrow(top_df) == 0) { cat("No significant co-enriched genesets.\n\n"); next }
    gs <- setNames(
      lapply(top_df$pathway, function(pw) msig_gs[[coll_name]][[pw]]),
      stringr::str_trunc(abbreviate_pathway(top_df$pathway), 45)
    )
    uc <- extract_ucell_scores(mpn_processed_hsc_fullcc, gs, umap_name = "umap.nn")
    for (g in names(gs)) {
      print(plot_ucell_umap(uc, g))
      cat("\n\n")
    }
  }
}
```

## Explore the enriched mCh+ erythroid neighbourhood

In general, the clusters representing the erythroid lineage show a pattern of depletion of both mCh+ and mCh- cells. However, a small neighbourhood displaying the opposite pattern stands out at early erythroid stage. Cluster 3 is isolated and analysed here using the same limma and detection-model pipelines as the main analysis.

```{r ery-setup}
ERY_CLUSTERS   <- c("3")   # candidate early erythroid; see also "9", "7"
da_res_ery_pos <- da_res_pos_all %>% filter(sNN_pca.SCT_30_res.0.9 %in% ERY_CLUSTERS)
```

```{r ery-limma}
sub_ery_pos    <- build_sub_expr(nhexpr, da_res_ery_pos, milo_hsc_obj)
gstats_ery_pos <- pergene_lfc_regression(sub_ery_pos)
```

```{r ery-detection}
ery_det_pos <- build_detection_substrate(milo_hsc_obj, da_res_ery_pos, subset.row = gene_subset)
det_ery_pos <- detection_lfc_model(ery_det_pos, adjust_depth = TRUE)
```


## miloDE — neighbourhood-level DE {#sec-milode}

Neighbourhood-level differential expression tested with `miloDE::de_test_neighbourhoods()` across three contrasts: mCh+ vs WT, mCh- vs WT, and mCh+ vs mCh-. Each neighbourhood is a cell × KNN graph community; DE is run within each neighbourhood to localise expression changes to specific UMAP regions.

```{r milode-load, eval=FALSE}
tar_load(milo_within_ngb_pos_de)
tar_load(milo_within_ngb_neg_de)
tar_load(milo_within_ngb_pos_neg_de)
#use the p-value corrected across genes since I didn't run cross-hoods p-value correction
milo_within_ngb_pos_de$pval_corrected_across_nhoods <- milo_within_ngb_pos_de$pval_corrected_across_genes

hood_annot <- miloR::annotateNhoods(
  milo_hsc_obj,
  da.res      = milo_hsc_da$mChPos_vs_WT$da_results,
  coldata_col = "sNN_pca.SCT_30_res.0.9"
)

milode_lst <- list(
  "mCh+ vs WT"   = milo_within_ngb_pos_de,
  "mCh- vs WT"   = milo_within_ngb_neg_de,
  "mCh+ vs mCh-" = milo_within_ngb_pos_neg_de
)
```

### miloDE gene logFC on neighbourhood graph

```{r, eval=FALSE}
miloDE::plot_DE_single_gene(milo_hsc_obj,
                            milo_within_ngb_pos_de,
                            gene = "Klf1",
                            layout = "umap.nn",
                            alpha =1) &
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red")
```

### DE magnitude per neighbourhood {.unnumbered}

Number of DE genes (`n_DE_genes`) and neighbourhood-specific DE genes (`n_specific_DE_genes`) plotted on the Milo UMAP. Each dot is a neighbourhood; size reflects neighbourhood size.

::: panel-tabset
```{r milode-magnitude, eval=FALSE, results="asis", fig.height=5, fig.width=10}
for (comp in names(milode_lst)) {
  cat("##", comp, "\n\n")
  de_stat     <- miloDE::convert_de_stat(milode_lst[[comp]])
  stat_de_mag <- miloDE::rank_neighbourhoods_by_DE_magnitude(de_stat)

  p1 <- miloDE::plot_milo_by_single_metric(
    milo_hsc_obj, stat_de_mag,
    colour_by  = "n_DE_genes",
    layout     = "umap.nn",
    size_range = c(1.5, 3),
    edge_width = c(0.2, 0.5)
  ) + scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "# DE genes", option = "turbo")

  p2 <- miloDE::plot_milo_by_single_metric(
    milo_hsc_obj, stat_de_mag,
    colour_by  = "n_specific_DE_genes",
    layout     = "umap.nn",
    size_range = c(1.5, 3),
    edge_width = c(0.2, 0.5)
  ) + scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "# specific\nDE genes", option = "turbo")

  print(patchwork::wrap_plots(p1, p2, nrow = 1))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```
:::

### Genes up/down across neighbourhoods {.unnumbered}

::: panel-tabset
```{r milode-updown, eval=FALSE, results="asis", fig.height=5, fig.width=6}
for (comp in names(milode_lst)) {
  cat("##", comp, "\n\n")
  p <- milode_lst[[comp]] %>%
    filter(!gene %in% sex_degs) %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    summarise(up_nbh   = sum(logFC > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
              down_nbh = sum(logFC < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    ggplot(aes(down_nbh, up_nbh, label = gene)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, color = "grey") +
    geom_point(size = 0.5) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = . %>% filter(down_nbh > 1000 | up_nbh > 1000),
      size = 3
    ) +
    labs(title = comp,
         x = "# neighbourhoods down-regulated",
         y = "# neighbourhoods up-regulated") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11)
  print(p)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```
:::

### Top DE genes per neighbourhood {.unnumbered}

For each contrast, the top genes by frequency of significant DE across neighbourhoods (padj \< 0.05, \|logFC\| \> 1).

::: panel-tabset
```{r milode-top-genes, eval=FALSE, results="asis"}
for (comp in names(milode_lst)) {
  cat("##", comp, "\n\n")
  top_genes <- milode_lst[[comp]] %>%
    dplyr::filter(pval_corrected_across_nhoods < 0.05,
                  abs(logFC) > 1) %>%
    dplyr::count(gene, name = "n_sig_nhoods") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(n_sig_nhoods)) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 50)

  if (nrow(top_genes) == 0) { cat("No significant genes.\n\n"); next }
  print(htmltools::tagList(
    DT::datatable(top_genes, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                  caption = paste("Top DE genes —", comp),
                  options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE))
  ))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```
:::

```{r milode-cleanup, eval=FALSE}
rm(milo_within_ngb_pos_de, milo_within_ngb_neg_de,
   milo_within_ngb_pos_neg_de, milode_lst, hood_annot); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

## Enrichment analysis based on gene expression

```{r, eval=FALSE}
ranks    <- setNames(da_res$logFC, as.character(da_res$Nhood))   # order nhoods by LFC
det_nh   <- sub$X>0               # genes x nhoods (detected?)
pathways <- apply(det_nh, 1, function(r) names(ranks)[r])# one nhood-set per gene
spec <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(pathways, ranks, minSize = 5)     # NES per gene = specificity
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
ranks    <- setNames(da_res$logFC, as.character(da_res$Nhood))   # order nhoods by LFC
pathways <- apply(sub$X, 1, function(r) r %>% sort %>% tail(300) %>% names, simplify = FALSE)# one nhood-set per gene
spec <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(pathways, ranks, minSize = 5)     # NES per gene = specificity
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
cap <- 100
ranks    <- setNames(da_res$logFC, as.character(da_res$Nhood))   # order nhoods by LFC
pathways <- apply(sub$X, 1, function(r){
  nz <- r[r>0]
  if(length(nz) > cap) nz <- nz %>% sort %>% tail(cap)
  names(nz)
  },
simplify = FALSE)# one nhood-set per gene
spec <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(pathways, ranks, minSize = 5)     # NES per gene = specificity
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
da_res <- milo_hsc_da$mChPos_vs_WT$da_results

cap <- 100
ranks    <- setNames(da_res$logFC, as.character(da_res$Nhood))   # order nhoods by LFC
pathways <- apply(sub$X, 1, function(r){
  nz <- r[r>0]
  if(length(nz) > cap) nz <- nz %>% sort %>% tail(cap)
  names(nz)
  },
simplify = FALSE)# one nhood-set per gene
spec <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(pathways, ranks, minSize = 5)     # NES per gene = specificity
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
da_res <- milo_hsc_da$mChPos_vs_WT$da_results

q_cutoff <- 0.9
ranks    <- setNames(da_res$logFC, as.character(da_res$Nhood))   # order nhoods by LFC
pathways <- apply(sub$X, 1, function(r){
  q_r <- r[r>=quantile(r, q_cutoff)]
  names(q_r)
  },
simplify = FALSE)# one nhood-set per gene

lengths(pathways) %>% table
spec <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(pathways, ranks, minSize = 5)     # NES per gene = specificity
```

Center of mass prioritization of genes

```{r, eval=FALSE}
E   <- sub$X[, da_res$Nhood]
tot <- Matrix::rowSums(E)
com <- ifelse(tot > 0, as.vector(E %*% da_res$logFC) / tot, NA)   # all genes, O(genes x nhoods)

```
